claim: Louvre timed-slot booking is mandatory for every visitor, reservable up to 90 days ahead, and slots sell out days in advance during summer.
quote: Timed-slot booking is mandatory for every visitor — reserve up to 90 days ahead. During summer, slots sell out days in advance.
note: summary synthesised across official + travel guide results

claim: From 14 January 2026 the Louvre introduced dual pricing: €22 for EEA residents and €32 for non-EEA visitors, a 45% rise for international guests.
quote: Effective Date: January 14, 2026. Non-EEA Visitors: The price increases by 45%, rising from €22 to €32. The increase applies specifically to visitors from outside the European Union, Iceland, Norway, and Liechtenstein.

claim: The Louvre's board decided in late November 2025 to raise ticket prices 45% for visitors from outside the EEA, the museum's first dual-pricing system.
quote: Louvre Hikes Ticket Prices by 45 Percent

claim: The 2026 Paris Museum Pass costs €85 (2-day), €105 (4-day) and €125 (6-day); both the Louvre and Musée d'Orsay still require a separate free timed reservation even with the pass.
quote: €85 for a 2-day (48-hour) pass, €105 for a 4-day (96-hour) pass, €125 for a 6-day (144-hour) pass. If you are planning to visit the Louvre museum using the Paris Museum Pass, you will need to pre-book a free time slot in advance.

claim: The Centre Pompidou closed on 22 September 2025 for a five-year renovation and will not reopen until 2030, with major works starting April 2026.
quote: The Centre Pompidou closed on 22 September 2025 for a major five-year renovation. Major renovation work will start in April of 2026. Reopening is planned for 2030.

claim: During its closure the Centre Pompidou continues programming off-site, with the Grand Palais hosting major Pompidou exhibitions and a Massy site opening autumn 2026.

From 10 March 2026 until summer 2028 the Musée d'Orsay renovates its reception areas while staying open with modified access routes; reservation is mandatory on the first Sunday of each month except for pass holders.
quote: From 10 March 2026 until summer 2028, the Musée d'Orsay will undertake major renovation of its reception areas. During the works, the museum will remain open to the public during its usual opening hours, though access routes will be temporarily modified.

claim: Rijksmuseum adult admission is €25, sold only online with a mandatory timed start time; under-18s are free and I Amsterdam City Card holders enter free but must still book a slot.
quote: All visitors are required to book a start time. Amsterdam City Card I: Free admission. Current Adult Price: €25
note: official page lists €25 adult and mandatory timed entry

claim: Tate Modern entry is free, but its blockbuster 'Frida: The Making of an Icon' (25 June 2026–3 January 2027) is a ticketed timed-entry show at £25 adult / £5 for ages 12-18, free for members.
quote: Tickets to the exhibition cost £25 for adults and £5 for children aged 12-18. Frida: The Making of an Icon opens on 25 June 2026 and runs until 3 January 2027. Advance booking is recommended.

claim: National Gallery London exhibitions use demand pricing — e.g. Zurbarán (to 23 Aug 2026) is £20 off-peak Sun-Thu and £22 Fri-Sat, under-18s free, with weekend and opening-week slots prone to selling out.
quote: Standard admission starts at £20 on off-peak Sunday to Thursday dates and rises to £22 on Fridays and Saturdays, with under 18s admitted free.

claim: National Gallery exhibition tickets are typically released about two months before opening, with members getting priority booking and popular slots selling out.
quote: tickets are usually released around 2 months before a show opens, and members of the Gallery receive priority booking for all new exhibitions.

claim: Rijksmuseum timed tickets regularly sell out for the most popular morning and weekend slots, so advance online booking is essential in peak season.
quote: Do Rijksmuseum tickets ever sell out? I Booking tips
